output.problem: Minimum wage earners face a rising cost of living but are largely outside conditional cash transfer programs meant for indigent households, while local MSMEs face thin margins and weak demand. The bill addresses both with one regular subsidy, delivered through digital wallets and spendable only in local MSMEs.
output.problem_quote: This measure addresses both problems with a single intervention: a direct, regular, and digitally delivered subsidy to minimum wage earners and their families

rows.target_quote: Every Qualified Family shall receive an annual Program Subsidy of Twelve Thousand Pesos (P12,000.00)

comparator.quote: THE SPECIFIC AMOUNTS SHALL BE FORMULATED IN CONSULTATION WITH THE DEPARTMENT OF BUDGET AND MANAGEMENT (DBM)
comparator.title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11310, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps) ACT”

rows.differences: HB No. 10219 leaves the amount and frequency of cash assistance to program guidelines set in consultation with the DBM, based on PIDS recommendations and taking into account inflation, poverty thresholds and available appropriations; this bill fixes P12,000 a year in the law.
rows.why: A fixed statutory amount cannot be adjusted to fiscal space or inflation without amending the law.
rows.tradeoffs: Setting the amount by guidelines gives fiscal flexibility but less certainty to beneficiaries than a fixed amount.
rows.gap: The number of qualified families, and so the annual requirement, is not stated.

rows.target_quote: There is hereby created a special fund, to be known as the PAMANA Trust Fund, to be maintained by the Bureau of the Treasury and administered by the DSWD

comparator.quote: The amount necessary for the initial implementation of this Act shall be charged against the current appropriations of the DTI, DICT, DA, and participating agencies.
comparator.title: AN ACT ESTABLISHING A NATIONAL DIGITAL MARKETPLACE AND E- COMMERCE SUPPORT PROGRAM FOR LOCAL PRODUCERS, PROVIDING DIGITAL, LOGISTICAL, FINANCIAL, AND CAPACITY- BUILDING ASSISTANCE TO MICRO, SMALL, AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES (MSMEs), FARMERS, FISHERFOLK, ARTISANS, AND COOPERATIVES, AND APPROPRIATING FUNDS THEREFOR

rows.differences: HB No. 9497 funds its program from the current appropriations of the implementing agencies and then the annual GAA; this bill creates a non-reverting trust fund from earmarked revenues, with the GAA covering any deficiency.
rows.why: Earmarking revenues and exempting the Fund from reversion reduce the flexibility of the General Fund and Congress's annual review of the program.
rows.tradeoffs: Regular appropriations keep the program within the annual budget process but make its funding less predictable than an earmarked fund.
rows.gap: Whether the earmarked revenues are already allocated under existing laws could not be established.

rows.target_quote: shall maintain a registry of Minimum Wage Earners based on payroll, SSS contribution, and other employment records

comparator.quote: THE DSWD SHALL MAINTAIN A CENTRALIZED DATABASE OF ALL SOCIAL PROTECTION PROGRAMS
comparator.title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11310, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps) ACT”

rows.differences: HB No. 10219 keeps one centralized DSWD database of all social protection programs and beneficiaries, with real-time data sharing with the DOLE and other agencies; this bill sets up a separate DOLE registry that the DSWD cross-matches.
rows.why: A separate registry may duplicate the DSWD's existing beneficiary registries; the DOLE data could instead feed one social protection database.
rows.tradeoffs: One database reduces duplication and fraud but depends on data-sharing arrangements across agencies.

rows.target_quote: There is hereby established the Pambansang Agapay sa Pamilya at Maliliit na Negosyo (PAMANA) Program, to be administered by the Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD)

comparator.quote: SHALL BE CONSOLIDATED, FUNDED, AND IMPLEMENTED THROUGH THE PANTAWID PAG-ASA PROGRAM
comparator.title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11310, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps) ACT”

rows.differences: HB No. 10219 requires new social amelioration programs to be consolidated and implemented through one DSWD program under unified guidelines; this bill creates a separate program with its own fund, rules and oversight.
rows.why: A stand-alone program adds to the number of cash assistance programs the DSWD runs, each with its own targeting and delivery.
rows.tradeoffs: Consolidation simplifies delivery and monitoring but may blur the program's distinct focus on minimum wage earners and local MSMEs.

rows.target_quote: The DTI, in coordination with local government units (LGUs), shall establish a simplified accreditation and onboarding system for MSME merchants

comparator.quote: LGUs shall, by ordinance, encourage the adoption of digital payment capabilities by merchants within their jurisdictions
comparator.title: AN ACT PROMOTING THE ADOPTION OF DIGITAL PAYMENTS FOR FINANCIAL TRANSACTIONS OF THE GOVERNMENT AND ALL MERCHANTS

rows.differences: HB No. 9692 relies on LGU ordinances and incentives to bring merchants onto digital payments, with capacity building from the BSP, DTI, DILG and DICT; this bill gives the DTI a dedicated accreditation and onboarding system at no cost to merchants.
rows.why: A dedicated accreditation system is needed to enforce the bill's restriction to local MSMEs.
rows.tradeoffs: A program-specific system is easier to control but adds an administrative layer for the DTI and LGUs.

rows.target_quote: A Joint Congressional Oversight Committee is hereby created to review the implementation of this Act.

comparator.quote: shall be composed of fourteen (14) members
comparator.title: AN ACT EXPANDING THE PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps), AMENDING FOR THE PURPOSE REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11310, OTHERWISE KNOWN AS THE “PANTAWID PAMILYANG PILIPINO PROGRAM (4Ps) ACT”

rows.differences: HB No. 10219 sets the oversight committee's composition and requires a periodic review of the program's impact; this bill creates a committee without its composition, powers or a review period.
rows.why: Defining the committee's composition and a periodic impact review would make oversight workable and support decisions on continuing the program.
rows.tradeoffs: A defined review adds reporting work for the DSWD but gives a basis for adjusting or ending the program.

duplications.quote: The DSWD shall cross-match the DOLE registry against the Listahanan, the 4Ps registry, or their successor registries

cost_notes.why: A recurring P12,000 a year for every qualified family, with no cap on the number of families.

cost_notes.item: Section 8 (Digital Wallet Onboarding and Financial Inclusion)
cost_notes.why: Free wallets, cash cards and offline payment solutions for every head of family.

A new registry updated quarterly, with an appeals process.

memo_part.heading: On the amount of the subsidy
paragraphs: 4.1 Section 5 of HB No. 10648 fixes the subsidy at P12,000 a year per qualified family, released in monthly tranches of P1,000. It may be noted that a fixed statutory amount cannot be adjusted to inflation or to the available fiscal space without amending the law. In this regard, may we recommend that the amount and frequency of the subsidy be set in the implementing guidelines, in consultation with this Department and based on available appropriations, similar to Section 8 of HB No. 10219, with a periodic review of its adequacy.

memo_part.heading: On the funding of the program
paragraphs: 4.2 Section 12 creates the PAMANA Trust Fund, sourced from earmarked revenues, including part of the value-added tax on digital services and of mining revenues, future excise taxes, excess GOCC dividends and privatization proceeds, with amounts that do not revert to the General Fund. It may be noted that earmarking revenues for a special fund reduces the flexibility of the national government to allocate resources according to its priorities and limits the annual review of the program through the budget process.

4.3 In this regard, may we recommend that the requirements of the program be included in the budget of the DSWD in the annual General Appropriations Act, subject to the availability of funds, similar to Section 14 of HB No. 9497, instead of a non-reverting trust fund.

memo_part.heading: On the identification of beneficiaries and program placement
paragraphs: 4.4 Section 9 tasks the DOLE to maintain a separate registry of minimum wage earners, which the DSWD cross-matches against the Listahanan and the 4Ps registry, while Section 4 establishes the Program as a stand-alone DSWD program. To avoid another beneficiary database and another cash assistance program with separate targeting, may we recommend that the DOLE data feed into the DSWD's existing social protection database, and that the Program be implemented within the DSWD's existing social protection framework, similar to Sections 11 and 14 of HB No. 10219.

memo_part.heading: On the oversight committee
paragraphs: 4.5 Section 11 creates a Joint Congressional Oversight Committee without stating its composition, powers or a period for review. May we recommend that its composition be defined and that it conduct a periodic review of the program's impact, similar to Section 18 of HB No. 10219, to inform decisions on its continuation.
